title: The British Museum
description: explore two million years’ worth of human history and culture.

title: The Victoria & Albert (aka the V&A)
description: ever-evolving collection with amazing outfits, glittering jewellery, intricate mosaics and ancient sculptures. (Also home to the oldest museum café in the world.)

title: The V&A East Storehouse
description: a dizzying collection of items in a ‘storehouse’ format, with guests able to request to view certain items.

title: The V&A East
description: one of London’s newest museums, with exhibitions and artwork dedicated to creativity’s power to bring change.

title: The Science Museum
description: a free museum dedicated to the miracle of technological progress.

title: The Design Museum
description: a celebration of all things in contemporary design (the name gives it away, right?)

title: The Natural History Museum
description: learn about dinosaurs, wildlife, venomous insects, earthquakes and more.

title: The Wellcome Collection
description: a museum-cum-library that connects the worlds of science, medicine, life, and art.

title: Horniman Museum & Gardens
description: an impressive collection of weird and wacky objects from across the globe, courtesy of Frederick John Horniman, as well as an impressive garden and a nature trail.

title: Sir John Soane’s Museum
description: a preserved, historic Holborn townhouse, absolutely packed to the brim with artwork and rare and random artefacts.

title: Queer Britain
description: the UK’s first and only museum dedicated to LGBTQ+ history.

title: The Vagina Museum
description: “the world’s first bricks and mortar museum dedicated to vaginas, vulvas and the gynaecological anatomy.”

title: Queen’s House
description: a stunning building in the heart of Greenwich that is full of art, and often hosts special events and tours for free.

title: Tate Britain
description: home to a vast a permanent collection of historic British art.

title: Tate Modern
description: one of the most popular modern art galleries in the world, housed with an immense, striking building.

title: The Serpentine Galleries
description: a duo of galleries in leafy park locations, accompanied by the Serpentine Pavilion – an annual architectural artwork.

title: The National Gallery
description: one of London’s most iconic gallery buildings, featuring centuries of jaw-dropping artworks.

title: National Portrait Gallery
description: over 220,000 portraits, from the 8th century to the present day.

title: White Cube Gallery
description: a duo of galleries showcasing stunning and often mind-bending contemporary art.

title: The Wallace Collection
description: a hidden gem of a museum with “unsurpassed masterpieces of painting, sculpture, furniture, arms and armour, and porcelain.”

title: Whitechapel Gallery
description: a ‘locally embedded’ gallery that showcases artwork from around the globe, “to make contemporary art accessible and exciting to the widest possible audiences”.

title: Somerset House
description: home to a “multidisciplinary cultural programme” that spans art exhibitions, cultural pop-ups, immersive experiences, and more.

title: Saatchi Gallery
description: one of the city’s most exciting contemporary art galleries, with a particular focus on emerging artists.

title: William Morris Gallery
description: “Home to the world’s most significant collection of William Morris’s work.” (temporarily closed for renovation)

title: Dulwich Picture Gallery
description: “the world’s first purpose-built public art gallery…. [with] a collection of over 600 European masterpieces”

title: BFI National Archive
description: not quite a museum or a gallery, but worth mentioning for its impressive collection of film and television, with over 95,000 titles.

title: The National Poetry Library
description: home to the largest public collection of modern poetry in the world.

title: Petrie Museum of Egyptian Archaeology
description: home to one of the largest collections of Egyptian artefacts in the world.

title: British Library
description: it’s a bit of a push to call a library a museum, but it is one of the largest libraries in the world. It’s home to the Magna Carta and handwritten Beatles lyrics among countless other works on some 400 miles of shelves.

title: The Old Blue Last
description: catch regular free gigs, ranging from jazz to indie rock, doo-wop, and experimental noise, at this Shoreditch boozer.

title: The Royal Academy of Music
description: there are regular classical performances here throughout the year, with plenty of free options.

title: Top Secret Comedy Club
description: with past, and potential, acts ranging across Jack Whitehall, Joanne McNally, Omid Djalili, and Simon Amstell, the £1 booking fee for an otherwise free comedy gig is well worth it.

title: The Blues Kitchen
description: self-styled as “London’s very own home of Blues and Rock’n’Roll music,” you can catch free live gigs at The Blues Kitchen almost every night.

title: Borough Market
description: officially the best food market in the world.

title: Walthamstow Market
description: the longest outdoor street market in Europe.

title: Horizon 22
description: the highest free public viewing platform in all of Europe.

title: The Garden at 120
description: a rooftop garden with stunning views

title: St. Paul’s Cathedral
description: marvel at it from outside, or you can take a peek inside for free by attending a church service, or the evening Choral Evensong.

title: Trafalgar Square
description: what are they going to do? Demand a ticket for hanging out on a public plaza? Not a chance! Explore one of London’s most iconic sights and spot the famous lion statues.

title: South Bank
description: go for a wander along the Thames and enjoy the sights, smells, and sounds of London.

title: Wellington Arch
description: one of London’s most iconic monuments, but you’ll be charged if you want to go inside and climb to the top.

title: Houses of Parliament
description: UK residents can visit for free by arranging it through your local MP or a member of the House of Lords.

title: Changing of the Guard
description: head to Buckingham Palace and you’ll get to see this legendary occurrence, completely for free.

title: Westminster Cathedral
description: “a Catholic Cathedral like no other [and] a supreme achievement of art,” and free to visit!

title: Tower Bridge
description: wander across one of the world’s most famous bridges, or marvel at it from the shore or another bridge (such as London Bridge).

title: Tower of London
description: you’ll need a ticket to enter, but you can certainly visit the site and take a look at the impressive building and moat from the outside.

title: Chinatown
description: even if you’re not tempted to stop in at one of the many eateries and restaurants, Chinatown is well worth a wander around.

title: Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
description: a 520-acre spot that’s well worth a wander around.

title: Greenwich Peninsula Art Trail
description: a free art trail that is home to statues by Damien Hirst.

title: Sightseeing Walking Tour Of London
description: don’t care about seeing inside the attractions? We’ve found the most efficient sightseeing walking tour of London.

title: Secret London Walking Tours
description: explore more of London with our walking tours and guides to various parts of the city.

title: Barbican Estate
description: a truly awe-inspiring Brutalist estate in London, with plenty to see as you wander around.

title: Highgate Cemetery
description: the resting place of 170,000 people, including Karl Marx and George Eliot.

title: Abbey Road
description: your chance to recreate that iconic album artwork by The Beatles at the zebra crossing.

title: Battersea Power Station
description: the disused Power Station has transformed into one of London’s hottest shopping, dining and leisure destinations, with plenty of sights to check out.

title: Platform 9 and 3/4
description: magic up a photo op at King’s Cross station.

title: The Diana Princess of Wales Memorial Walk
description: celebrate the life of the ‘People’s Princess’ along this 7-mile memorial walk around central London.
venue_name: The Diana Princess of Wales Memorial Walk

title: St. Dunstan In The East
description: a ruined church that has been overtaken by nature; now a serene hideaway from bustling London, in the heart of the City.

title: Hyde Park
description: perhaps London’s most famous park; a Grade I-listed spot with an impressive lake, gardens, galleries, statues, a hidden waterfall, and more.

title: Walthamstow Wetlands
description: over 13 miles of paths across an untamed, wildlife-friendly site.

title: Kyoto Garden
description: a unique, Japanese-style landscape; an oasis of calm in the heart of Kensington’s Holland Park.

title: Postman’s Park
description: home to a truly affecting memorial, commemorating ‘ordinary’ people who died while acting heroically.

title: Regent’s Park
description: home to a secret garden with special areas designed for meditation and stunning statues scattered throughout.

title: Richmond Park
description: home to grazing deer and the The Isabella Plantation, which turns pink when the azaleas bloom.

title: Dalston Eastern Curve Garden a charming plant
description: filled oasis in Dalston.
venue_name: Dalston Eastern Curve Garden a charming plant

title: Queen Elizabeth Rooftop Garden
description: a hidden garden atop the Queen Elizabeth Hall… with over 200 wild native plants, a luscious lawn, views across London and the Roof Garden Bar & Kitchen.

title: Leake Street
description: add your own artworks or marvel at the graffiti masters at one of London’s only legal graffiti spots .

title: Buddhapadipa Temple
description: the UK’s first Buddhist temple, featuring 4 acres of gorgeous gardens, an 18th-century lake, and a cafe serving up delicious Thai breakfasts

title: Eel Pie Island
description: a private island full of artists and history, accessible to the public on a handful of days a year.

title: The Totteridge Yew
description: the oldest tree in London, with an estimated age between 1,000 and 2,000 years old.

title: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
description: a traditional Hindu temple, standing some 70 feet high and carved entirely out of stone.

title: Cross Bones Graveyard
description: tranquil shrine to paupers and prostitutes, which honours the city’s ‘outcast dead’.

title: London Mithraeum
description: a painstaking restoration of an ancient Roman temple, once a site of worship for a cult dedicated to the god Mithras. Find it beneath the headquarters of media giant Bloomberg.

title: The Seven Noses of Soho
description: a trail of nose sculptures hidden around Soho, as a satirical nod towards the surge in surveillance as CCTV was installed around the area in 1997.

title: Britain’s Smallest Police Station
description: tucked away in a corner of Trafalgar Square is a teeny tiny, blink-and-you’ll-miss-it police station with a fascinating history.

title: Gods Own Junkyard
description: a neon wonderland full of glimmering neon artworks and signs.

title: The Sherling Backstage Walkway
description: take a peek behind the scenes and watch sets and props being made at the National Theatre from high above.

title: 25 Cannon Street aka the upside down St Paul’s park
description: a charming little pocket-sized park with an oval reflection pool that perfectly frames an upside-down view of the dome of St Paul’s.
